chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Musallī, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUbayd, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about the ghusl (ritual washing) of the deceased. He said: A cloth is placed over him, then his private part is washed, and wudu (ablution) of salat is performed for him. Then his head is washed with lote leaves and ushnan, then with water and camphor, then with pure water, and seven sound leaves from the lote tree are placed in the water.

key_terms.الْأُشْنَانِ: a cleansing plant material used for washing
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor mixed with water in the washing process
key_terms.خِرْقَةٌ: a cloth placed over the deceased during washing
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: the wudu performed in the manner of prayer ablution

ai.seo_question: How is the ghusl of the deceased performed according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the procedure for the ghusl (ritual washing) of the deceased, including covering the body, washing the private part, performing wudu (ablution), and washing with sidr, camphor, and pure water. It reflects a jurisprudential ruling on funerary purification in Shia fiqh.
